Crime in Chicago has been tracked by the Chicago Police Department's Bureau of Records since the beginning of the 20th century.
The city's overall crime rate, especially the violent crime rate, is higher than the US average.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crime_in_Chicago#cite_note-1)Gangs in Chicago have a role in the city's crime rate.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crime_in_Chicago#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crime_in_Chicago#cite_note-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crime_in_Chicago#cite_note-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crime_in_Chicago#cite_note-5) Chicago gangs prefer to do business with Indiana gun stores because Indiana has significantly weaker laws than Illinois.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crime_in_Chicago#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crime_in_Chicago#cite_note-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crime_in_Chicago#cite_note-8)

The number of homicides in Chicago hit a 25-year high in 2021,[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crime_in_Chicago#cite_note-9) but reached a five-year low in 2024 with a continued downward trend into 2025.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crime_in_Chicago#cite_note-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crime_in_Chicago#cite_note-11)
The scatterplot displays the reported crimes in Chicago for each week in 2024 _[citation needed_]
Chicago saw a major rise in violent crime starting in the late 1960s. Homicides in the city peaked in 1974, with 970 homicides when the city's population was over three million, resulting in a homicide rate of around 29 per 100,000, and again in 1992, with 948 homicides when the city had fewer than three million people, resulting in a homicide rate of 34 per 100,000 citizens.
After 1992, the homicide count steadily decreased to 415 murders by the mid-2000s, a reduction of over 50 percent. In 2021, there were 805 homicides recorded, representing a homicide rate of 29.8 per 100,000. The year of 2022 saw a decline in homicides, followed by another 15% decline in 2023, ending the year with a total of 621.

Chicago experienced major rises in the 1920s, in the late 1960s, and in the 2020s,[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crime_in_Chicago#cite_note-13) a decline in overall crime in the 2000s,[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crime_in_Chicago#cite_note-14) and then a rise in murders in 2016.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crime_in_Chicago#cite_note-Chicago_Police_Annual_Report_2017-15) Murder, rape, and robbery are the most common violent crimes in the city, and occurrences of such incidents are documented by the Chicago Police Department and indexed in annual crime reports.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crime_in_Chicago#cite_note-:1-16)

By 2010, Chicago's homicide rate had surpassed that of Los Angeles (16.3 per 100,000), and was more than twice that of New York City (7.0 per 100,000).[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crime_in_Chicago#cite_note-19) By the end of 2015, Chicago's homicide rate rose to 18.6 per 100,000. Chicago recorded 779 homicides in 2020. This figure represents an increase of more than 55% over 2019. On the Fourth of July weekend 2021, at least 100 people, mostly African-American, were shot, 18 of them fatally.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crime_in_Chicago#cite_note-21)
